narrative.intro: Massachusetts Institute of Technology obligated $916M in federal contracts in FY2026 to date. The university won 26 awards this fiscal year to date, with an average award size of $35.2M. Obligations fell 36.5% year over year. Past fiscal-year totals show a peak pattern: FY21 $1.1B, FY22 $1.1B, FY23 $1.4B, FY24 $1.5B, FY25 $1.4B, and FY26 $916M. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Biotechnology) is by far the largest market, with $809M obligated in FY2026 to date. A secondary research market, Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), accounted for $107M. These figures are contract obligations except where award-value notation applies in the largest-awards and expiring-contracts tables. Current-year totals are partial, representing fiscal year to date activity. This snapshot highlights heavy concentration in R&D work and a meaningful year-over-year decline in obligations for FY2026 to date.

sections.heading: What markets drive Massachusetts Institute of Technology federal revenue?
sections.body: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Biotechnology) is the largest market at $809M in FY2026 to date. A secondary market, Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), totaled $107M. These two NAICS-market entries account for the bulk of FY2026 to date obligations. The work profile shows strong concentration in physical, engineering, and life-sciences R&D.
